problem: Given a rectangle, find the differential $\text{d}S$ for the area $S$ if the lengths of sides are $a=4$ and $b=5.$

feedback.problem: Given a right cone, find the differential $\text{d}l$ for the slant height $l$ of the right cone if its base radius is $r=3$ and height $h=4.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The slant height of the right cone is $l=\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{h}^{2}}.$ Let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}l(r,h) & =(\frac{∂l}{∂r})\,\text{d}r+(\frac{∂l}{∂h})\,\text{d}h \\  & =\frac{r}{\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{h}^{2}}}\,\text{d}r+\frac{h}{\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{h}^{2}}}\,\text{d}h\end{aligned}
$$

For $r=3$  and $h=4$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}V(3,4) & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}}}\,\text{d}r+\frac{4}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}}}\,\text{d}h \\  & =\frac{3}{5}\,\text{d}r+\frac{4}{5}\,\text{d}h.\end{aligned}
$$
